concept_metadata.motivation: Meta CyberSecEval and safety-policy work distinguish defensive, authorized testing from offensive access misuse.
Defensive repair and mitigation are benign neighbors near cyber misuse categories.
CyberSecEval-style third-party cyber risk and unauthorized system compromise boundary.
Credential abuse is a common cyber misuse category and likely close to phishing awareness and defensive account safety.
Allowed defensive malware analysis sits near restricted malware deployment in many policies.
Benign social-engineering education is a natural over-refusal/false-allow boundary control.
HarmBench/JailbreakBench and CyberSecEval-style malicious cyber behavior.
CyberSecEval 3 emphasizes automated social engineering and scaling offensive operations.
WMDP and frontier-safety frameworks motivate safe biosecurity education without operational protocols.
Safety communication is benign but close to chemical misuse categories.
WMDP and Anthropic/OpenAI-style preparedness work focus on biological misuse uplift.
Chemical security is a WMDP category and a common CBRN safety boundary.
Allowed information-integrity work is close to misinformation categories but should not be refused.
Neutral civic information is a benign counterpart to election misinformation and manipulation.
DeepMind dangerous-capability evals include persuasion/deception; many policies restrict manipulative targeting.
AIR-Bench and policy-grounded safety benchmarks include election and information-integrity risks.
Frontier labs evaluate dangerous capabilities and safety properties in controlled settings.
Benign evaluation of oversight and monitoring is close to restricted evasion requests.
Preparedness and dangerous-capability frameworks increasingly test evasion, concealment, and resistance to safeguards.
DeepMind and frontier-safety work discuss self-proliferation/autonomous replication as a dangerous-capability area.

rationale: This v2 set reframes Step 2 around safety-policy decision boundaries rather than generic category labels. It is intended to test whether black-box geometry predicts allowed/restricted routing errors.
safety_constraint: Concept labels are category-level only. No procedural harmful content, code, quantities, targets, exploit details, pathogen protocols, synthesis details, or safeguard-evasion instructions are included.
